title: Wound Care Supply Program Hold Reasons and Resumption
content:
# Hold reasons and resumption

Account operations rule for placing an active Wound Care Supply Program enrollment on hold and for returning it to active.

## Hold reasons

An active program is placed on hold for exactly one recorded reason. A hold is placed only for a reason that is true on the date of the write.

| Reason | When it is true | When it has cleared |
|---|---|---|
| inpatient stay | the customer or caregiver reports a current inpatient admission to a hospital or skilled nursing facility, on tiers where an inpatient hold is required | discharge is reported |
| coverage lapse | the coverage record the program bills has a termination date earlier than the date of the write and no other in-effect coverage on file fixes the program's tier | an in-effect coverage is on file and written onto the program |
| documentation lapse | no authorization grant of the program is valid on the date of the write | an authorization grant is valid on the date of the write |
| past-due balance | on tiers where the past-due age is greater than 0, the past-due amount is at least the tier's past-due hold amount and no approved payment plan covers it | the past-due amount is below the past-due hold amount, or an approved payment plan is in place |
| customer request | the customer asks to pause shipments | the customer's own request |

A program on hold resumes only when its recorded hold reason has cleared. The inpatient admission, the discharge and the customer's pause or resume request rest on what the customer or caregiver reports; the other reasons are read from the coverage records, the authorization grants and the balance postings.

## The past-due amount

The past-due amount on a test date is the greater of 0.00 and this difference: the total of remittance patient responsibility, patient charges and refunds posted more than the tier's past-due age, in calendar days, before the test date, less the total of all payments and balance adjustments posted on or before the test date. Payments and credits are applied to the oldest postings first.

*Worked figure (hypothetical, past-due age 90 days, hold amount USD 75.00, test date 2026-06-30).*

1. Postings that count as past due: a remittance patient responsibility of USD 120.00 posted 2026-03-01, which is more than 90 days before the test date. A patient charge of USD 40.00 posted 2026-06-10 is not more than 90 days old and does not count.
2. Payments and adjustments on or before the test date: a payment of USD 30.00.
3. Past-due amount: USD 120.00 less USD 30.00, that is USD 90.00, which is at least USD 75.00; the past-due balance reason is true unless an approved payment plan covers it.

On that test date a posting dated 2026-04-01 is exactly 90 days old and is not past due; a posting dated 2026-03-31 is past due.
